colors._comment: There is NO input fill. `input_fill` / `input_yellow_fill` (#FFF2CC) were added and then removed: 411 tinted cells on the Smurfit case is a highlighter pass, not a reference model. `total_fill` is gone with them because it was a synonym for `answer_fill` while block subtotals actually carry `subsection_fill`, so the one name covered two different treatments. An editable cell is BLUE FONT and nothing else — see fill_semantics.

number_formats._comment: The ladder. One format per class of content, and every format the build emits appears here verbatim — these are the exact formatCode strings in xl/styles.xml, not a description of them. The old single `rate` key had to serve coupons AND spreads at once, which is why the 0.000% coupon format was specified here and absent from every emitted file.
number_formats.adjustment_delta_note: The AMOUNT format for the ADJUSTMENT block N:P only, and the reason it is a separate entry rather than a variant applied ad hoc. N:P is the middle term of A + B = C: it states what the transaction ADDS to the standalone case, not a third level standing beside the other two. Carrying plain `amount` there made a figure in P typographically identical to a figure in L, which is what left the adjustment columns reading as a third complete statement. The explicit leading `+` is what distinguishes a bridge column from a balance column; negatives keep the model's parentheses, so the pair reads +1,100 / (48). It is applied ONLY where the base format is `amount` — a percentage, multiple or rate in N:P restates the pro-forma ratio rather than the change in it, and a `+` there would misstate what the number is. THE ZERO SECTION IS DELIBERATELY STILL AN EN-DASH, NOT BLANK: see zero_and_uncalculated_must_not_converge. An en-dash says the row does not move, an empty cell says there is nothing there, grey says it was never computed; blanking the zero would collapse the first two and destroy the distinction. Resolver: scripts/build_dynamic_model.mjs :: setPeriodNumberFormat.

number_format_rules.closed_set_note: No numFmt may reach styles.xml that is not listed in number_formats. A raw 0.0000 and a bare 0 were in active use with nothing to say what they meant.
number_format_rules.zero_and_uncalculated_must_not_converge: The en-dash on white says the figure is zero; the grey fill says it was never computed. That distinction is the only thing telling a reader which is which, so grey is always a FILL and never a number format, and every format that can hold a computed zero carries an explicit zero section.

_comment: ONE FILL, ONE MEANING — and THE FILL CHANNEL BELONGS TO TOTALS.
#D9EAF7 used to be the total fill AND the input fill, so a subtotal row
and a cell the reader is meant to type over were the same colour: a real
provenance collision. A yellow input fill broke it, and was too loud —
411 tinted cells on one case. It is broken instead by giving fill to the
rank hierarchy ALONE (nothing on a component sum, #EFF5F9 on a block
subtotal, #D9EAF7 on an answer) and leaving every input unfilled. An
input has no fill to collide with, so the collision cannot recur by any
route.
CONSEQUENCE: blue font is now the ONLY thing marking an input, which
makes the provenance layer more load-bearing than before, not less.
`conditional_state.conditional_font_colour_forbidden` and the emitter's
partial-font-assignment rule are what protect it.
fill_semantics.white: ordinary body, formulas, calculated zero, and every COMPONENT SUM
fill_semantics.answer: answer rows only — roughly ten rows, never an input
fill_semantics.na_grey: intentionally not calculated or not applicable only
fill_semantics.input: NO FILL. An editable input is marked by blue font alone, wherever it sits. An input that is ALSO a total (a subtotal whose history is hardcoded) carries its own rank's fill, which is the row's identity and not an input marking.
fill_semantics.state_amber: conditional: revolver drawn in that year
fill_semantics.state_red: conditional: liquidity shortfall in that year

_comment: These are the values the DYNAMIC build emits, read back out of
xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml — not the geometry of the static template in
scripts/build_template.mjs. The whole block used to be a verbatim copy of
that template (freeze G16, B at 27, C:E at 9.75 and so on), which was
accurate for build_template.mjs and wrong for every model actually
shipped: seven of the eight width entries and the freeze row disagreed
with the emitted package.
freeze_pane is COMPILED OUTPUT, the same way physical rows are (see
total_ranks). patchFreezePane() freezes at G{period_row + 1}, so the row
moves the moment the row plan does; G16 is what period_row 15 compiles
to across every current case, period_row itself now being DERIVED from
the last visible acquisition-helper row immediately above the period
header. It now happens to AGREE with
template-contract.json's crh_consolidated.freeze_pane, and must still not
be linted against it: that profile describes the static template, which
freezes at G16 for reasons of its own, and the agreement is a coincidence
of row counts, not a shared rule. lint_contracts.mjs asserts
only the invariant that survives compilation — the split is at column G,
i.e. xSplit 6, leaving the label and terms block B:E visible.
layout.blank_rows_note: The former two-row gap now carries the visible acquisition operating-fraction and full-year EBITDA helpers. The period header remains on its frozen-authority row and no hidden support block is introduced.

block_titles._comment: `Standalone` / `Adjustment` / `Pro Forma` on the period-group row are CENTRED ACROSS their blocks by alignment, never by merging: horizontal=centerContinuous on every cell of G:L, N:P and R:U, with the text in the leftmost cell of each run. patchBlockTitleAlignment() writes it into the package, because format.horizontalAlignment is the fourth formatting call the writer accepts and emits nothing for — it rejects centerContinuous outright and silently drops the values it does accept.

column_widths._comment: Column F is a gutter at width 2 in the dynamic build, so the old `F:L` key could not survive: it grouped a gutter with five period columns. A, F, M and Q are all narrow spacers, but only A, M and Q are BREAKS — see gutter_policy.
column_widths._label_column_comment: B was 39 (202.83pt usable at Calibri 8). An instrument row is the one label row that cannot overflow — C, D and E carry its currency, nominal and maturity — and the longest instrument name in the certification suite needs 224.36pt, so five labels were cut at the column edge on standard-maximal and Smurfit and two more sat within a point of it on AstraZeneca. Those names are source text and may not be shortened to fit, so the column carries them: 45 characters is 234.33pt usable, 4.4% clear of the widest. The width unit is the MAXIMUM DIGIT WIDTH of the workbook default font, fonts[0], which is why that font must be Calibri and not a substitute Excel does not have.

_comment: A NARROW COLUMN IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A BREAK. A, F, M and Q are all
width-1-or-2 spacers and were all treated as breaks, which is what cut
every band and every rule in two at column F.
F sits between the instrument TERM columns C:E and the PERIOD GRID from
G. Both sides of it belong to the SAME line item on the SAME basis — a
bond's currency and that bond's 2027 balance are two facts about one
row — so a fill or a rule that stops at F splits one row into two
halves with no reason to be apart, and leaves a section band reading as
a labelled block plus a detached rectangle over the period columns.
M and Q separate STANDALONE from ADJUSTMENT and ADJUSTMENT from PRO
FORMA: three different BASES of the same figure, which the reader must
never conflate. The white gap is what makes three column blocks read as
three column blocks, so it stays.
A is the sheet's left margin — nothing to its left to carry across to.
REVERSAL, RECORDED: `gutter_columns_must_remain_white` previously
included F and the build honoured it. Reviewer round 4, item C2,
approved carrying the formatting across F. This is a contract change,
not a tweak, and CARRY_THROUGH_GUTTERS in
scripts/build_dynamic_model.mjs is the single place it is implemented.
gutter_policy.terms_period_boundary_marked_by: the terms block's own vertical edges, not by a white gap — a vertical division belongs in a vertical channel

_comment: A BAND SPANS THE COLUMN BLOCKS ITS SECTION ACTUALLY USES.
The former `ranges` array carried PHYSICAL ROW NUMBERS (B4:L4, B16:L16 …)
and was stale on every current case — the control band is on row 3, not
row 4 — for exactly the reason total_ranks stopped listing rows: physical
rows are compiled output and never canonical. What is canonical is which
COLUMN BLOCKS a band covers.
Every statement section spans all three period blocks. The CONTROL
section does not: it is two panels, the model controls at B:C and the
acquisition case at N:P, with no period grid at all. Banded across all
blocks it emitted navy over G:L and again over R:U — ten columns of
section header over permanently empty sheet, marking nothing (reviewer
round 4, item B6). Filling a column block a section does not reach is a
claim the sheet cannot honour.
THREE RANKS OF TOTAL, keyed on the row's own SEMANTIC IDENTITY *AND THE
SECTION IT IS EMITTED INTO*.
This replaces the former `total_rows` and `subsection_rows` arrays, which
carried PHYSICAL ROW NUMBERS and so contradicted the architecture rule that
physical rows are compiled output and never canonical: insert one instrument
and every number in those arrays was wrong while still reading as
authoritative. Rank now resolves in scripts/lib/row_plan.mjs (totalRank,
groupSubtotalRank) from (row_id | semantic_role, section), and the emitter
looks the physical row up through the compiled plan.
WHY SECTION. The same line is legitimately an ANSWER where it concludes a
build-up and a STEP where it feeds one. `net_interest_expense` is the answer
of the interest schedule and a step on the income statement. Keyed on the id
alone it could only be one of the two, and the set — written from the debt
overlay's point of view — declared it an answer everywhere. The income
statement then gave the reader a double-ruled, answer-filled INTEREST line
with net income below it in a lighter treatment, while `adjusted_ebitda`,
`ebit` and `net_income` were not in the answer set at all.
BOLD IS NOT PART OF RANK ANY MORE — see `headline` below. Rank owns the
fill and the rules; narrative prominence is its own declared channel.
Subsection headers are likewise resolved from style_role, not listed here.

component_sum.meaning: closes a run of like items
component_sum.treatment: thin top rule over the number cells, NO FILL, BOLD
structural: every debt-group subtotal (Total Bonds / Bank Debt / Other Debt)

block_subtotal.meaning: closes a block of the model

answer.meaning: the figure the reader came for, IN THIS SECTION
answer.treatment: thin top rule, DOUBLE bottom rule, answer_fill, BOLD
_row_ids_comment: The flat union across sections, which is what a validator reading the
emitted file can check a fill against. `by_section` is the authority; this
list is derived from it and must stay its union.
`net_interest_expense` appears here because it IS the answer of the
interest schedule. It is NOT the answer of the income statement, and
answer.two_bases_terminate_identically: net_debt_company_reported and net_debt_company_reported_to_adjusted_ebitda take the SAME rank as their model-basis counterparts. The company-reported figure used to fall through to the block-subtotal default, so the formatting asserted that the model basis is the real number and the published one a footnote. They are two answers to the same question.

total_ranks.rule_spans_note: B:L is ONE run, not B:E plus G:L: the rule carries straight through gutter F (see layout.gutter_policy). It still breaks at M and Q, so a rank rule is three runs across the sheet and not one band — a rule that closes a run is not a grid. It also INCLUDES the label column B. It used to start at C — the key was `rule_spans_number_cells_only` — so a total's underline began a column and a half to the right of the total's own name and read as a property of the number block rather than of the line. B is a label column, not a gutter; A, M and Q are still white and unbordered.
total_ranks.adjacent_section_boundary: A block subtotal whose NEXT row opens a sub-section also takes a thin dark grey BOTTOM rule. subsection_fill is deliberately the same colour on both (see fill_semantics.subsection), so `Net Cash from Operations` and `Cash from Investing (CFI)` ran together into one two-line banner belonging to neither section. The closing rule separates them without either fill changing meaning. An answer row keeps its double rule.

_comment: SEMANTIC TOTALS AND SUBTOTALS ARE BOLD, UNIVERSALLY.
The trigger is the compiled rank, never a company name, label spelling or
physical row. This makes Revenue, Gross Profit, Operating Profit, PBT and
unfamiliar issuer-specific totals consistent without overfitting.
The ladders below add rare narrative prominence to a row that is not
otherwise a semantic total; they no longer restrict which totals are bold.
One job per channel:
rules (single / double / box)  arithmetic closure — where a sum ends
bold                           semantic totals plus declared headlines
fill                           rank hierarchy (total_ranks)
font colour                    provenance — never touched by any of this
Each entry is a LADDER, not a row id: the FIRST id present in the compiled
section wins and the rest are ignored. That is how the set adapts to what a
company actually reports — a case stating `operating_profit` bolds that
line, a case stating only `ebit` bolds that one, and neither is forced onto
a company presenting neither.
Chrome is not a headline and is not listed: section bands, the period
header, the control block and label-only sub-block titles (row_type ===
'header') are bold because they are chrome, not because they are prominent.
A NUMBERED row carrying style_role 'subsection' — a consolidated parent
with its constituents indented beneath it — is not chrome or a ranked
total. It remains ordinary-weight and unbanded so the
indented children read as the auditable composition of that parent.
chrome_is_bold_and_is_not_a_headline: the period header and period group header
the control block and the acquisition case block
the debt schedule's *_header rows, group headers and term headers

_comment: STANDING PROJECT RULE: the compiler and the validator must not trust the
same classification blindly. The ladders above are the AUTHORITY. The
check `answer-rank-is-earned-not-asserted` in validate_style_tokens.mjs
derives a second, independent signal from the emitted file alone — how
many other rows' formulas READ this row — and holds the answer rank to
it. It shares nothing with the declaration.
It is what catches the original defect: on the income statement,
`net_interest_expense` is read by NOTHING (reach 0) and has four ranked
rows below it, yet carried the answer fill. In the interest schedule the
same id is read by the income statement, and there it is the answer.
independent_validator.signal: reach = distinct rows whose formulas reference this row, ranges expanded
independent_validator.rule: a row may carry answer_fill only if reach >= 1, OR it is a ratio row (nothing ever sums a multiple or a margin), OR no other ranked row lies below it in its own section

_comment: TWO BASES, TWO PANELS, SEPARATED BY A BLANK ROW.
The model-basis box and the company-reported box used to SHARE AN EDGE, so
two frames touching read as one region with a line through the middle
rather than as two statements of the same figure on two bases. A blank row
sits above the model-basis panel and between the two panels. Positions are
derived from the compiled row plan (row_plan.mjs :: PANEL_SPACER), never
hardcoded: the spacer consumes a row number and lands in no index, so no
emitter can address it and every downstream row still resolves through the
plan.
spacer_rows: one blank row above `company_reported_header`, when the company panel exists

_comment: Fill only, on cells that already exist, driven by the control block.
A conditional rule may set fill, border, bold/italic and number format. It
may NEVER set font colour on a body cell: font colour is the provenance
layer and a rule that overrides it silently destroys it.
Structure does not depend on state — no rule here sets a border, so every
rank rule and every double underline stays put when a toggle flips.
Control addresses resolve from rowPlan.controls and are never hardcoded.

circularity_off.effect: interest schedule FORECAST cells take na_fill + italic; history untouched

maturity_roll_off.effect: maturity column and scheduled repayment rows read as suppressed

adjustment_columns_off.effect: N:P recedes; pro forma S:U stays live because A + B = C means it correctly equals standalone

rcf_drawn.effect: state_amber on ending_rcf, that year only

liquidity_shortfall.when: residual liquidity shortfall > 0 in that column
liquidity_shortfall.effect: state_red on liquidity_shortfall, that year only

broker_case_selected._comment: Replaces `broker_case_not_consensus`, which fired in ONE direction only. The old rule tinted the cell #EFF5F9 when the case was not Consensus and did nothing otherwise, so on the default case — five of the six certification cases — the control naming the entire forecast basis carried no mark at all, and in the other state it carried the same near-white that every subsection header and block subtotal wears. A control that is silent in its default state cannot announce which state it is in.
broker_case_selected.when: always — the broker case control is tested in both directions
broker_case_selected.effect: toggle_off_fill when the control reads "Consensus", toggle_on_fill when anything has been selected over it. The underlying question is binary (has the market consensus been overridden), so it is answered in the same on/off vocabulary the two switches beneath it carry. Fill only: the cell is a hardcoded input and its blue font is its provenance, so neither rule sets a font colour even though a single-cell control rule would be permitted one.
broker_case_selected.selector_is_not_a_toggle: The broker case is a NAMED CHOICE out of a list, not a switch and not a magnitude, and it now has its own control treatment — centred and bold like a toggle field, blue like the input it is, and shrink-to-fit so a full house name or Forecast Waterfall remains inside the compact canonical control cell. See scripts/build_dynamic_model.mjs :: styleSelectorControl. It previously used the plain entry-field treatment, which left the most consequential control in the model as the quietest thing in the panel.

live_broker_case_row._comment: On the BROKERS sheet, not the Operating Model. Every candidate — one row per named broker, then Consensus, High and Low — was formatted identically, so nothing said which one the `Selected case` row had actually picked up.
live_broker_case_row.when: the candidate's own name in column B equals the live case
live_broker_case_row.effect: toggle_on_fill and bold, ACROSS THE WHOLE ROW on a DERIVED candidate (Consensus, High, Low) and on the NAME CELL ONLY on a named house. A derived row is calculated here and already carries subsection_fill end to end, so a conditional fill across the same span changes which rank colour it wears, not whether it wears one — that holds even where a pack supplies its consensus as a hardcode, because the fill is the ROW's identity and the blue font is that CELL's provenance. A named house's C:F cells are its own forecast and nothing else, and input_carries_no_fill means an input is marked by blue font and nothing else, so the mark stops at its name. The unselected alternatives are made subordinate by the live row gaining a mark, never by the others being greyed — na_fill means not calculated, and eight real broker forecasts are not that.
live_broker_case_row.cross_sheet_reference_spent_once: The live case is resolved into a single ordinary formula cell (Brokers!E2, green as a cross-sheet link) and every rule tests that same-sheet absolute. A conditional-format formula reaching across sheets is not reliably honoured through the writer and the LibreOffice pass, so it is spent once where it is robust rather than repeated in a rule on every candidate row.

_comment: Frames, not a grid. Every rule below either closes a run or draws a box
round a panel; none rules a body cell on all four sides. Gutter columns A,
M and Q stay white and unbordered, which is what makes the three period
blocks read as blocks. F is NOT one of them: it carries fills and rules
across (see layout.gutter_policy), so B:E and G:L are one run.
ORDERING, and it is not optional: a PARTIAL border assignment silently
clears the RIGHT perimeter edge of the range it touches while preserving
the left. Every box is therefore drawn AFTER every rule that crosses it,
and a panel's own header rule is drawn BEFORE its box.
borders.period_header_row: thin dark grey bottom rule per column block, breaking at the breaking gutters only
borders.standalone_forecast_boundary: thin dark grey left border at J, full model height
borders.controls: thin grey box around the control entry fields
borders.acquisition_controls: thin grey box around the acquisition entry fields
borders.instrument_terms: thin light grey box around C:E on the debt and interest schedules
borders.interest_assumptions: thin dark grey outer with thin internal divider
borders.section_close: thin dark grey bottom rule on the last row of each section, per column block
borders.subsection_close: thin dark grey bottom rule on a block subtotal whose next row opens a sub-section — see total_ranks.adjacent_section_boundary
borders.totals_hierarchy: see total_ranks — rank is carried by line weight, not by fill

_comment: AN ATTRIBUTE IS NOT A STEP IN THE ARITHMETIC, SO IT MUST NOT READ LIKE ONE.
C:E state what an instrument IS — currency, face value, maturity on the
debt schedule; rate type, coupon or spread, benchmark on the interest
schedule. Every column from G rightwards states what HAPPENS to it, period
by period, and that is the left-to-right flow the reader is meant to trace.
The terms carried the same upright Calibri 8 as the grid and column D
carried the same `amount` format as every period column, so a nominal
amount in D was typographically indistinguishable from a balance in J:
three columns of static reference data competing with the period grid at
the head of every row, all the way down both schedules.
The box round C:E says where the boundary IS. It cannot say which side of
it matters more, which is why the border alone left the block still reading
as four more columns of model (reviewer: 'columns C to E look very',
'boring'). The answer is not more ink on C:E but less weight.
instrument_terms.treatment: italic on the term VALUE cells; the header row keeps its upright bold
instrument_terms.why_italic: It is the vocabulary this sheet already uses for the same idea one axis over: a ratio row is italic because it is a READING of the arithmetic rather than a term in it (see styleStatementRow). A contract term is the same kind of thing. It recedes at a glance, costs no colour, no fill and no palette entry, and stays perfectly legible — an italic date is still a date.
instrument_terms.partial_font_assignment_required: Every one of these cells is a hardcoded input carrying BLUE and a few are formulas carrying black or green. A full font object would reset them all and destroy the provenance of the entire terms block. `{ italic: true }` merges, exactly as `{ bold: true }` does in applyTotalHierarchy, and assertFormulaProvenance() — which also assigns partially, `{ color }` alone — runs afterwards and reinstates the colours without disturbing the italic.
instrument_terms.alignment: currency, maturity, rate type and benchmark name are CENTRED; the two genuinely numeric terms — nominal amount and coupon — stay RIGHT, for the same reason the period columns do

indentation._comment: Real indentation: `alignment indent` on the label cell. Levels are DERIVED from the ref graph in scripts/lib/row_plan.mjs and never listed as physical rows, and they are written into the package by patchLabelIndents() because the writer accepts format.indentLevel and emits nothing.
indentation.leading_spaces_note: Two literal spaces inside the label string is content pretending to be style: invisible to any restyle, impossible to change globally, and it corrupts column-width measurement. row_plan strips them so the two cannot compound.
indentation.consolidated_line_constituent_note: A compiler-declared group parent sits at body level one and its explicit constituents sit at level two. Working-capital children may be blank and grey only when their forecast parent captures them; Change in Debt children remain live formula links on white cells.
